correctness.rationale: The model has exactly two independent age-geometric parent choices per vertex, with replacement, followed by simple-edge projection. A coupling with independent two-sided geometric-age choices changes only finitely many arrival edges almost surely, since sum_j 2q^j is finite. Stationary finite-range truncations give ergodic motif frequencies, and monotone/local-integrability bounds transfer to the untruncated graph for fixed q in (0,1). Each triangle has a unique youngest vertex, giving sum_(a,b>=1)2 p_a p_(a+b)(2p_b-p_b^2). Distinct older-neighbor count O and independent Poisson-binomial younger-neighbor count I yield E binom(O+I,2), giving the displayed rational t(q),w(q). Independently checked exact rational identities, t(3/10)=7854/23491 and w(3/10)=8123920/2560519, and symbolically checked t prime=-2PT/((1+q)^3(1+q+q^2)^2), c prime=-6PC/[numerator_w(q)]^2. Descartes one-sign-change plus endpoints proves unique roots 0.4204133882 and 0.2169310203 and distinct maxima. Checks corroborate the analytic fixed-q law, not uniform varying-q statements.

originality.rationale: The April 2025 exponentially preferential recursive tree has one parent and hence no ordinary triangles. Pachon–Stephenson 2025 uses affine-degree attachment with explicit triangle-closing, not independent exponential ages. Tang–Wang–Wu 2026 studies the exact with-replacement m-parent exponential-age law but its publicly accessible main theorem/abstract is on recurrence and random-walk collisions; no exact motif-density or competing optimizer formula was identified. Full text could not be inspected through public/OA routes, and authorized Oxford access reported disconnected VPN, so this exact-model priority risk remains. On available evidence the distinct rational motif maxima survive.
